name: Garrick Ironhand

loved: {item}. Hah! Now that's a gift worth the fire.
...{item}. You do know how to leave a man speechless.
liked: Good stuff. I'll put it to work.
disliked: {item}? What am I supposed to do with that?
hated: Get that away from my forge!
{item}. You're joking. Tell me you're joking.

arrival: Hrm. Smoke from a hearth, a village with a proper forge going up. Finally.
Name's Garrick. Smith, thirty years. My last town burned its own bridge, and I'm tired of walking.

arrival.say: I'll earn my keep. Hammer doesn't care where it falls. Room for one more?

reply: Good. Then you'll have the finest nails in the country.

choices.text: As long as you share your stories.
reply: Hah. Maybe after the second pint.

arrival: I'll find the anvil. Don't touch anything hot.
bouquet_accept: *He turns them over in thick, scarred hands, as if they might break.*
I'd like to see where this goes, {player}.
bouquet_reject: Flowers? Hah. That's... kind. But I don't know you well enough for that.
pendant_accept: That's... {player}, are you proposing to a blacksmith?
Yes. Aye, yes. Three days. I'll find a clean shirt.
pendant_reject: Whoa. Slow down, friend. Give an old smith more time.
wedding: *The village gathers by the hearth. Garrick is scrubbed so clean you almost don't recognise him.*
I don't do speeches. I do iron. So here's what I forged for you: a promise that doesn't bend.

wedding.say: Will you take this old smith, {player}?

reply: Then that's the best day's work I've ever done.
Hah! Then that's the best day's work I've ever done.

wedding: *The village cheers. Somebody bangs a pot on an anvil.*

greetings.say: Birthday, hm? Don't make a fuss. ...But thanks for coming by.
Need something mended, or just looking?
Good iron, good ale, good company. Rare combination.
You've got a good eye for quality, {player}. I notice these things.
Cold out. Perfect weather for working metal.
Saturdays, I drink. Don't tell the anvil.
Hey, you. Good to see you.
I made something for you, but it isn't done yet. Don't ask.
Still can't believe my luck. Don't tell the anvil that either.

script: Don't stand so close to the quench barrel. ...Hmph. You've got steady feet. Most don't.

script.say: Tell me, can you swing a hammer?

reply: *He guides your hands onto the hammer and shows you the rhythm: tap, tap, strike.*
There. You've got it.
Fair. Watching's half of learning.
It is. It's also the only honest kind.

script: *He holds a sword snapped clean in two.* Forty years, my father's blade never failed. Cracked on the first day I wore it.

script.say: I've been trying to mend it for a week. The metal won't take the weld.

choices.text: Metal remembers. It can be mended.
reply: ...Maybe it can. Maybe I just needed someone to say it.

choices.text: Maybe it's time to retire it.
reply: Retire it. Hrm. Maybe you're right. Doesn't feel right, though.
Stubborn. Quiet. Taught me everything but how to say what I feel. Maybe I'll tell you more some day.

script: *Evening. Garrick nurses a mug alone in the corner of the tavern.*
Sit, {player}. I don't usually talk about this.
I left the capital because I got too good. They wanted me to forge weapons for a war I didn't believe in.

script.say: So I walked away. Left my forge, my name, everything. Do you think that makes me a coward?

reply: *He stares into his mug for a long moment.* ...Thanks, {player}. I needed to hear that.
Aye. I'm here now. That's something.
*His jaw tightens.* Hrm. Fair. Not what I wanted to hear.

script: Close the door. I want to show you something.
*He unwraps a long blade, mirror-bright, with a faint wave in the steel like water.*
My masterwork. Took me three winters. I never sold it.

script.say: I want you to have something from this forge. Pick: a tool for working, or a keepsake for remembering.

reply: *He hands you a freshly forged iron pickaxe.* Use it hard. That's how it says thank you.
*He presses a small iron horseshoe into your palm.* Luck. Keep it close.

script: *Garrick is waiting by the forge at dusk, a small bundle in his hands.*
The broken blade. I finally figured out how to mend it. I didn't weld it back, {player}. I made it into something new.
*He opens his palm. A plain iron ring, glinting, made from the old sword.*

script.say: I'm no good with words. But every strike of this hammer thought of you. Is that clumsy?

choices.text: It's the best thing anyone's ever said.
reply: *He exhales for the first time in a minute.*
Then I did right.
Hmph. Flattery. ...Keep going.

script: *He sets his father's mended sword in your hands. It's whole now, the old crack a silver line.*

script.say: I spent my life afraid of passing down anything. Turns out I just needed someone to pass it to.

reply: I know you will.
Together. Aye. I like the sound of that.
